params.description: Base normalized view of Stack Overflow question posts: one row per question_id with core question attributes (title, body, counts, dates, owner, score, tags, etc.).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve question-level metadata and textual fields (title, body, tags) for reporting or joining into higher-level analyses. | Filter or select questions by creation_date, score, view_count, tags, owner_user_id, or accepted_answer_id. | Serve as the canonical question input when composing aggregates (answer counts, comment counts, favorites) or joining to user records (one-to-one) or pre-aggregated answer/comment metrics. | Build dashboards or features that require one row per question (e.g., list of questions with score and counts).
params.output_schema: question_id: unique identifier of the question post (derived from posts_questions.id) | title: question title text (derived from posts_questions.title) | body: full question body HTML/text (derived from posts_questions.body) | accepted_answer_id: id of the answer post marked accepted for this question (derived from posts_questions.accepted_answer_id) | answer_count: number of answers recorded on the question (SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.answer_count AS INT64)) | comment_count: number of comments on the question (derived from posts_questions.comment_count) | community_owned_date: timestamp when question became community owned (derived from posts_questions.community_owned_date) | creation_date: timestamp when question was created (derived from posts_questions.creation_date) | favorite_count: number of times question was favorited/bookmarked (SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.favorite_count AS INT64)) | last_activity_date: timestamp of last activity on the question (derived from posts_questions.last_activity_date) | last_edit_date: timestamp of last edit to the question (derived from posts_questions.last_edit_date) | last_editor_display_name: display name of last editor if anonymous (derived from posts_questions.last_editor_display_name) | last_editor_user_id: user_id of last editor if registered (derived from posts_questions.last_editor_user_id) | owner_display_name: display name of the question owner if anonymous (derived from posts_questions.owner_display_name) | owner_user_id: user_id of the question owner if registered (derived from posts_questions.owner_user_id) | post_type_id: internal post type identifier (derived from posts_questions.post_type_id) | score: integer score (upvotes-downvotes) of the question (derived from posts_questions.score) | tags: raw tags string (often in <tag1><tag2>... format) (derived from posts_questions.tags) | view_count: number of times the question was viewed (SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.view_count AS INT64))
params.metric: answer_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.answer_count AS INT64) -- stored counter on the question row (non-aggregated, point-in-time snapshot) | favorite_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.favorite_count AS INT64) -- stored counter on the question row | view_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_questions.view_count AS INT64) -- stored counter on the question row | score = posts_questions.score -- stored integer score on the question row | comment_count = posts_questions.comment_count -- stored counter on the question row
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-question (questions are unique by question_id) and users_base is one-row-per-user; joining attaches user attributes without duplicating question-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to answers_base on accepted_answer_id = answers_base.answer_id — safe for enriching questions with the accepted answer row (one-to-one) because accepted_answer_id references at most one answer; does not multiply question rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to post_votes_agg on question_id = post_votes_agg.post_id — safe if post_votes_agg is pre-aggregated to one row per post (as an AGG sibling). Because post_votes_agg is an aggregate per post, joining will not duplicate measures in this view. | do NOT join directly to answers_base on question_id = answers_base.parent_id (or any answers table that is one-to-many) without re-aggregation, because answers_base contains one row per answer and will multiply question rows (answer_count and other question-level counters would be duplicated). Instead, join to an aggregated answers view (e.g., question_answer_counts or an aggregation of answers_base grouped by parent_id) to preserve correct cardinality. | do NOT join directly to comments_base on question_id = comments_base.post_id (or any comments table that is one-to-many) without first aggregating comments to one row per question (e.g., comments_count per post), because that would duplicate question rows and inflate question-level measures. | when you need per-question aggregates computed from many-side tables, use the provided AGG sibling views (question_answer_counts, post_votes_agg) or aggregate answers/comments first: e.g., LEFT JOIN (SELECT parent_id AS question_id, COUNT(*) AS answers_from_answers_base FROM answers_base GROUP BY parent_id) USING(question_id). This ensures measures on questions_base remain 1:1 and are not multiplied by the join. | if joining to reshaped/tag exploded views (question_tag_exploded), be aware that those are one-to-many (one question -> many tag rows). Only join when you intend to explode questions by tag; otherwise aggregate tags into arrays or join to a tag-aggregated view to remain cardinality-safe. | joins that are safe without re-aggregation: joins to one-row-per-user views, one-row-per-answer when joining by accepted_answer_id, and pre-aggregated per-question metric views. Joins that are unsafe without aggregation: any direct join to answers, comments, or tag-exploded views keyed on question_id because they are one-to-many.

questions_base.description: Normalized projection of posts_questions with cleaned numeric casts and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical questions relation for downstream joins, aggregations, or time-series. Converts nullable numeric-like STRING fields to INT64 when possible and exposes key metadata. | Use for: time-series of question creation or activity; top questions by score/view_count/answer_count; analysis of accepted answers by question attributes; joins to answers, comments, votes, users

answers_base.name: answers_base
answers_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  title,
  body,
  accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  comment_count AS comment_count,
  community_owned_date AS community_owned_date,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) AS favorite_count,
  last_activity_date AS last_activity_date,
  last_edit_date AS last_edit_date,
  last_editor_display_name AS last_editor_display_name,
  last_editor_user_id AS last_editor_user_id,
  owner_display_name AS owner_display_name,
  owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  parent_id AS parent_id,
  post_type_id AS post_type_id,
  score AS score,
  tags AS tags,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`

params.description: Answers about individual answer posts (one row per answer_id) from the Stack Overflow answers table, exposing post fields (body, score, owner, counts, dates, tags, etc.).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve attributes or metadata for a specific answer (by answer_id) or a set of answers (filter by creation_date, owner_user_id, score, parent_id, tags, etc.). | Compose rollups or aggregates about answers (counts, average score, recent activity) by first selecting/ filtering this view and then aggregating. | Join answers to their parent question (questions_base) to combine question and answer attributes. | Enrich answers with user information by joining to users_base on owner_user_id or last_editor_user_id. | Filter or rank answers per question when combined with question_answer_counts or answers_ranked_by_score_per_question (use those after appropriate join/aggregation).
params.output_schema: answer_id: unique id of the answer post (derived from posts_answers.id as answer_id) | title: post title string (derived from posts_answers.title) | body: full post body/markup (derived from posts_answers.body) | accepted_answer_id: id of accepted answer for the parent question (derived from posts_answers.accepted_answer_id) | answer_count: SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) — the answer_count field from posts_answers cast to INT64 (derived from posts_answers.answer_count) | comment_count: number of comments on this post (derived from posts_answers.comment_count) | community_owned_date: timestamp when post became community owned (derived from posts_answers.community_owned_date) | creation_date: timestamp when the answer was created (derived from posts_answers.creation_date) | favorite_count: SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) — favorites count cast to INT64 (derived from posts_answers.favorite_count) | last_activity_date: timestamp of last activity on the post (derived from posts_answers.last_activity_date) | last_edit_date: timestamp of the last edit (derived from posts_answers.last_edit_date) | last_editor_display_name: display name of the last editor if present (derived from posts_answers.last_editor_display_name) | last_editor_user_id: user id of the last editor if present (derived from posts_answers.last_editor_user_id) | owner_display_name: display name of the post owner (derived from posts_answers.owner_display_name) | owner_user_id: user id of the post owner (derived from posts_answers.owner_user_id) | parent_id: id of the parent post (the question id this answer is attached to) (derived from posts_answers.parent_id) | post_type_id: numeric post type id (derived from posts_answers.post_type_id) | score: numeric score (derived from posts_answers.score) | tags: tags text for the post (derived from posts_answers.tags) | view_count: SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) — view count cast to INT64 (derived from posts_answers.view_count)
params.metric: answer_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_answers.answer_count AS INT64) -- provided as-is but casted to INT64 | favorite_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_answers.favorite_count AS INT64) -- provided as-is but casted to INT64 | view_count = SAFE_CAST(posts_answers.view_count AS INT64) -- provided as-is but casted to INT64 | score = posts_answers.score -- post score (integer/number) provided directly | comment_count = posts_answers.comment_count -- comment count provided directly
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base on answers_base.parent_id = questions_base.question_id — safe because answers_base is one-row-per-answer and questions_base is one-row-per-question; joining answers -> questions will not duplicate answer rows (many answers -> one question) but joining questions -> answers would multiply question rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on answers_base.owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — safe because users_base is one-row-per-user; this attaches user attributes to each answer without duplicating answer measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on answers_base.last_editor_user_id = users_base.user_id — safe for the same reason as above. | do NOT join answers_base directly to any one-to-many child (for example comments_base, question_tag_exploded, or any raw votes table) without first aggregating the child to one row per answer_id, because such a join would duplicate answer rows and thus multiply counts/metrics (score, view_count, favorite_count, comment_count). | If you need totals from a one-to-many table (e.g., comments_base rows per answer), first aggregate the one-to-many table to answer_id with the desired metrics (COUNT(*) AS comments_on_answer, SUM(...) AS ...) and then LEFT JOIN that aggregated result to answers_base on answer_id — this preserves answer-level cardinality and prevents metric duplication. | Be careful when joining to post_votes_agg or question_answer_counts (AGG views): those are aggregate views. If they are aggregated at the question level, joining them to answers_base on parent_id = question_id is safe only if you intend to repeat the same question-level metric for each answer. If you want per-answer metrics, use a per-answer aggregate. Explicit guidance: | - Joining answers_base -> post_votes_agg on answer_id = post_votes_agg.post_id is safe if post_votes_agg is aggregated by post_id (one row per post). | - Joining answers_base -> question_answer_counts on answers_base.parent_id = question_answer_counts.question_id will attach question-level counts (same value for every answer of that question); this is safe but note the semantics (question-level metric replicated per answer). | When composing further aggregations over answers_base (e.g., compute average score per question), group by the appropriate parent key (parent_id) and aggregate columns from answers_base. Do not join a one-to-many table first and then aggregate without deduplication. | If joining to reshaped/tag exploded views like question_tag_exploded, which are one-to-many (one question -> many tag rows), avoid direct join to answers_base on parent_id = question_id unless you intend answers to be repeated per tag. Instead either (a) aggregate tags into arrays at the question level and join to questions_base then to answers_base, or (b) pre-aggregate the tag-exploded view to one row per question with the metric you need and then join.

answers_base.description: Normalized projection of posts_answers with cleaned numeric casts and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical answers relation for downstream joins, aggregations, or to link back to questions via parent_id. | Use for: linking answers to their parent questions; top answers by score/comment_count/view_count; analysis of answerer activity over time or by reputation

users_base.name: users_base
users_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  display_name,
  about_me,
  SAFE_CAST(age AS INT64) AS age,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  last_access_date AS last_access_date,
  location,
  reputation AS reputation,
  up_votes AS up_votes,
  down_votes AS down_votes,
  views AS views,
  profile_image_url,
  website_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`

params.description: Base user profile information: one row per user_id describing display name, profile texts, activity timestamps, location, reputation and vote/view counts.
params.when_to_use: Look up profile attributes for a specific user_id or set of user_ids (display_name, about_me, location, profile_image_url, website_url). | Filter users by age, reputation, creation_date, last_access_date, up_votes, down_votes, or views. | Join user profile attributes to posts (questions/answers) or aggregated metrics when you need one-row-per-user context. | As the starting point for user-level aggregates (e.g., counts of posts per user) or for building user-level cohorts (e.g., active users since a date).
params.output_schema: user_id: unique identifier for the user; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.id | display_name: the user's display name; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.display_name | about_me: free-text 'about me' profile field; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.about_me | age: SAFE_CAST(age AS INT64) — user's reported age as integer (nullable if invalid/missing); derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.age | creation_date: timestamp when the user account was created; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.creation_date | last_access_date: timestamp of the user's last access; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.last_access_date | location: free-text location field from the profile; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.location | reputation: integer reputation score; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.reputation | up_votes: integer count of up votes received on the profile; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.up_votes | down_votes: integer count of down votes received on the profile; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.down_votes | views: integer count of profile views; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.views | profile_image_url: URL to the user's profile image; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.profile_image_url | website_url: URL the user put in their profile; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users.website_url
params.metric: user_id = id (identity key, not an aggregate) | display_name = display_name (attribute) | about_me = about_me (attribute) | age = SAFE_CAST(age AS INT64) (type-casted attribute) | creation_date = creation_date (attribute) | last_access_date = last_access_date (attribute) | location = location (attribute) | reputation = reputation (attribute) | up_votes = up_votes (attribute) | down_votes = down_votes (attribute) | views = views (attribute) | profile_image_url = profile_image_url (attribute) | website_url = website_url (attribute)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base on questions_base.owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — safe because users_base is one-row-per-user, and questions_base is one-to-many (many questions per user). If you need user-level measures (e.g., number of questions), use questions_base aggregated (COUNT(* ) GROUP BY owner_user_id) before joining to avoid duplicating user_base rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to answers_base on answers_base.owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — safe for adding answer-level rows, but to retain one-row-per-user you must pre-aggregate answers (e.g., COUNT, SUM) by owner_user_id before joining; otherwise answers will multiply users_base rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to comments_base on comments_base.user_id = users_base.user_id — comments are one-to-many per user; pre-aggregate comment metrics by user_id when you want to keep one row per user. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to post_votes_agg on post_votes_agg.post_owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — post_votes_agg is already aggregated by post owner; if post_votes_agg is one-row-per-user (confirm its grain), direct join is safe. If it's one-row-per-post-owner-per-post, aggregate to user level first. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to question_answer_counts on question_answer_counts.owner_user_id = users_base.user_id — question_answer_counts is an aggregate; if it is one-row-per-question or one-row-per-user, verify its grain. To avoid multiplication, join only if question_answer_counts is aggregated to user-level or aggregate it (SUM) by owner_user_id first. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to question_tag_exploded is NOT safe if used directly (question_tag_exploded explodes tags causing many rows per question). Do NOT join users_base directly to question_tag_exploded without aggregating tags back to user-level (e.g., ARRAY_AGG or COUNT DISTINCT per user) because that would multiply user rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_with_user or answers_ranked_by_score_per_question must consider their grain: questions_with_user is a JOIN that likely produces one row per question (including user attributes) — joining users_base back to it on user_id would duplicate the user's row for each question. To preserve one-row-per-user, aggregate those question/answer views by owner_user_id first. | general rule: users_base is strictly one-row-per-user (user_id primary key). Any join to a one-to-many detail table/view (questions, answers, comments, exploded tags, ranked answers) will multiply users_base rows. To compose safely, either (a) aggregate the detail to user_id before joining, or (b) join users_base to the detail only when you intend to expand to one-row-per-detail (i.e., accept duplication of user attributes across detail rows).

users_base.description: Cleaned users projection preserving identity and profile metrics. Use for joining post or comment authors to profile attributes like reputation and location. | Use for: join users to posts/comments; user retention and activity analyses; demographic or reputation-based segmentation

comments_base.name: comments_base
comments_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS comment_id,
  text AS text,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  post_id AS post_id,
  user_id AS user_id,
  user_display_name AS user_display_name,
  score AS score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments`

params.description: Provides one row per StackOverflow comment with its identifiers, text, creation date, associated post and user, user display name, and score.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve or filter comments by id, post_id, user_id, creation_date, score, or text content. | Join comments to post-level data (questions or answers) when you need comment-level detail attached to a single post row each comment references. | Aggregate comment-level metrics (counts, average score, min/max dates) grouped by post_id, user_id, or time windows. | Compose higher-level metrics that start from individual comments (e.g., comments per post, average comment score per user) by re-aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: comment_id: unique identifier for the comment; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.id | text: body text of the comment; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.text | creation_date: timestamp when the comment was created; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.creation_date | post_id: id of the post (question or answer) this comment is attached to; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.post_id | user_id: id of the user who made the comment (may be NULL for anonymous); derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.user_id | user_display_name: display name shown for the comment author (may be present for anonymous contributions); derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.user_display_name | score: integer score (votes) on the comment; derived from bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.score
params.metric: comment_id = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.id) | text = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.text) | creation_date = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.creation_date) | post_id = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.post_id) | user_id = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.user_id) | user_display_name = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.user_display_name) | score = identity(bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments.score) | derived_metrics_guidance = when computing aggregates, re-aggregate from this one-row-per-comment grain; e.g., comments_per_post = COUNT(comment_id) GROUP BY post_id; avg_comment_score_per_user = AVG(score) GROUP BY user_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base on post_id = question_id — safe only when you know post_id references a question row (one-to-one on question id) because comments are one row per comment and joining attaches each comment to at most one question row; measures at comment grain are not duplicated by this join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to answers_base on post_id = answer_id — safe when post_id references an answer row; each comment maps to at most one answer, so comment-level measures remain unduplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on user_id = user_id — safe because users_base is one row per user_id; joining enriches comment rows with user attributes without duplicating comment measures. Note: user_id can be NULL; outer joins may be needed to preserve anonymous comments. | cardinality-UNSAFE warning: do NOT join directly to any one-to-many child of comments (if such existed) without re-aggregation, because that would multiply comment rows and thus duplicate comment-level measures. | cardinality-UNSAFE warning: do NOT join to post_votes_agg or question_answer_counts without attention to join keys and aggregation direction. post_votes_agg is an aggregate over votes; joining aggregated vote rows keyed by post_id is safe if post_id is the join key and post-level aggregation matches intent (it will attach vote aggregates to every comment on that post but will not duplicate comment rows). However, if post_votes_agg is aggregated at a different grain (e.g., per post+vote_type) ensure you join on the same grouping keys or re-aggregate post_votes_agg to post_id first to avoid duplication. | composition notes: when combining comments_base with higher-grain aggregations (post-level or user-level), choose the aggregation direction explicitly: either (a) aggregate comments_base to the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY post_id) then join to other aggregates on that same grain, or (b) join comments_base to a one-row-per-post or one-row-per-user view (questions_base, answers_base, users_base) which are safe because they are one-row-per-id. Avoid joining comments_base to views that are one-to-many relative to post_id or user_id without re-aggregation.

comments_base.description: One row per comment with preserved linkage to post and commenter. Useful for counting comments per post or analyzing comment timelines. | Use for: comment counts per post or per user; comment activity over time; join comments to posts and users

post_votes_agg.name: post_votes_agg
post_votes_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  post_id,
  vote_type_id,
  COUNT(1) AS votes_by_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes`
GROUP BY
  post_id,
  vote_type_id

params.description: Aggregated counts of votes by vote type for each post (one row per post_id and vote_type_id).
params.when_to_use: Count how many votes of each vote_type_id a specific post received. | Break down vote distribution across vote types for a set of posts. | Compose with post-level entities (questions/answers) to attach vote-type counts to posts and then re-aggregate to other grains (e.g., per-question totals or per-user totals) without re-scanning the votes table. | Build further aggregations by joining on post_id and/or vote_type_id and then summing votes_by_type (safe when joins do not create duplicate post_id x vote_type_id rows).
params.output_schema: post_id: ID of the post that received the vote — derived from votes.post_id in the base table. | vote_type_id: Type identifier of the vote (integer code indicating e.g., upvote/downvote/accept) — derived from votes.vote_type_id in the base table. | votes_by_type: Count of vote records for that (post_id, vote_type_id) pair — derived as COUNT(1) over votes grouped by post_id and vote_type_id.
params.metric: votes_by_type = COUNT(1) GROUP BY post_id, vote_type_id  -- counts rows in bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes for each post_id x vote_type_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base (or answers_base) on post_id — safe because this view is one row per (post_id, vote_type_id). Joining to a one-row-per-post dimension (questions_base or answers_base) will not duplicate votes_by_type as long as those post tables have at most one row per post_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_with_user on post_id — safe if questions_with_user is one row per post_id (it is a JOIN view that should preserve one row per question). votes_by_type will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on user_id only after first joining questions_base (or answers_base) to bring a single user_id per post_id — safe because the post->user relation is one-to-one in that path; ensure you join votes_agg -> questions_base (post_id) then questions_base -> users_base (user_id). | do NOT directly join to one-to-many siblings (e.g., question_tag_exploded) on post_id without re-aggregation — joining votes_agg to a multi-row-per-post view will multiply the votes_by_type counts. If you need totals at the tag level, first aggregate votes_by_type to post-level sums (SUM(votes_by_type) GROUP BY post_id) and then join to question_tag_exploded. | do NOT join to comments_base (or other views that may have multiple rows per post_id) without re-aggregating votes_agg — joining as-is will produce duplicated votes_by_type across the multiple comment rows. Instead, either aggregate comments or aggregate votes_agg to the desired grain before joining. | Safe pattern to get per-post total votes across all vote types: SELECT post_id, SUM(votes_by_type) AS votes_total FROM post_votes_agg GROUP BY post_id — then join that result to any one-row-per-post view. | Safe pattern to get per-question totals for answers: first map answer post_ids to their parent question_id via answers_base (one row per answer), then aggregate: SELECT a.question_id, SUM(pv.votes_by_type) FROM post_votes_agg pv JOIN answers_base a ON pv.post_id = a.post_id GROUP BY a.question_id — this is safe because answers_base is one row per answer post_id and the aggregation SUM(...) removes duplication introduced by answer->question many-to-one mapping. | If composing by vote_type_id (e.g., to pivot or filter specific vote types), joining on both post_id and vote_type_id preserves the original grain and is safe as long as the other side is at most one row per (post_id, vote_type_id).

post_votes_agg.description: Aggregated vote counts by post_id and vote_type_id. Useful to compute breakdowns of vote types per post (upvotes, accepted, etc.) or to join to posts for total vote measures. | Use for: vote-type distribution per post; total votes by summing votes_by_type; correlate votes with score/comment_count/view_count

question_answer_counts.name: question_answer_counts
question_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  parent_id AS question_id,
  COUNT(1) AS answers_total,
  AVG(score) AS avg_answer_score,
  MAX(score) AS max_answer_score,
  MIN(creation_date) AS first_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  parent_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  parent_id

params.description: Per-question (parent_id) aggregate counts and summary scores for answers: total number of answers, average and max answer score, and earliest answer creation date.
params.when_to_use: Get counts and score summaries for all answers to a given question (one-row-per-question). | Join question-level answer metrics into question-level datasets (e.g., enrich questions with answers_total, avg_answer_score). | Filter or rank questions by answer activity or by score-based answer summaries (e.g., questions with no answers_total or low avg_answer_score). | Serve as a reusable aggregated foundation when composing further aggregations or features at the question grain (avoid re-aggregating answers directly).
params.output_schema: question_id: the question post id corresponding to posts_answers.parent_id (renamed parent_id AS question_id). This is the grouping key / grain: one row per question_id. | answers_total: COUNT(1) of rows in bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers for that parent_id. Derived from posts_answers (COUNT(1)). | avg_answer_score: AVG(score) of answers for that parent_id. Derived from posts_answers.score (AVG(score)). | max_answer_score: MAX(score) of answers for that parent_id. Derived from posts_answers.score (MAX(score)). | first_answer_creation_date: MIN(creation_date) of answers for that parent_id (earliest answer creation date). Derived from posts_answers.creation_date (MIN(creation_date)).
params.metric: answers_total = COUNT(1) over posts_answers grouped by parent_id | avg_answer_score = AVG(posts_answers.score) grouped by parent_id | max_answer_score = MAX(posts_answers.score) grouped by parent_id | first_answer_creation_date = MIN(posts_answers.creation_date) grouped by parent_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base (or any question-level view) on questions_base.id = question_answer_counts.question_id — safe because question_answer_counts is one-row-per-question_id, so its measures will not be duplicated when joining to a true one-row-per-question dimension. | Safe to join to questions_with_user on questions_with_user.question_id = question_answer_counts.question_id because questions_with_user is a question-level JOIN that preserves one-row-per-question grain. | Safe to join to answers_ranked_by_score_per_question only if you join on (question_id AND rank = 1) or otherwise limit to a single answer row per question; joining to answers_ranked_by_score_per_question without restricting to one row per question may multiply rows and duplicate the aggregated measures. | Do NOT join directly to answers_base (or any raw answers table) on question_id without re-aggregating or otherwise preventing one-to-many expansion — answers_base is one-to-many (multiple answers per question), so a direct join will multiply question_answer_counts measures (e.g., answers_total) and produce incorrect totals. | Do NOT join to comments_base, post_votes_agg, question_tag_exploded, or other one-to-many reshaped tables on question_id (or post_id) unless you first aggregate those tables to one row per question_id or join using keys that guarantee one-row-per-question. For example, joining question_tag_exploded (which explodes tags into multiple rows per question) will duplicate question-level aggregates unless tags are aggregated back to question-level. | If you need combined measures from multiple one-to-many children (e.g., answers and comments), perform separate aggregations at the child level (one-row-per-question) and then join those aggregated results together on question_id — this preserves correctness because each side is one-row-per-question. | When composing further aggregations on top of this view (e.g., average answers_total by owner or by tag), ensure you join to a dimension that aggregates to the grouping key you intend (e.g., questions -> owner_user_id) and use appropriate GROUP BY on that higher-level key; do not assume question_answer_counts can be rolled up across duplicate question keys introduced by downstream joins.

question_answer_counts.description: Per-question aggregated answer statistics (count of answers, avg answer score, max answer score, first answer time). Use to analyze question response quality and speed. | Use for: questions with fastest first answer; relation between question attributes and answer quality; filtering questions by number or quality of answers

question_tag_exploded.name: question_tag_exploded
question_tag_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  TRIM(tag) AS tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(COALESCE(q.tags, ''), r'<([^>]+)>')) AS tag

params.description: Explodes Stack Overflow question tags so each row is one question_id + single tag (one row per question-tag relationship).
params.when_to_use: List or count distinct tags used by questions. | Filter or group questions by individual tag (e.g., find question IDs for a given tag). | Join tags back to question-level aggregates (e.g., answer counts, scores) without carrying concatenated tag strings. | Build tag-level aggregates (e.g., questions per tag, average answers per tag) by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: question_id: the question's primary key id (derived from posts_questions.id) | tag: a single tag string extracted from the posts_questions.tags field (whitespace-trimmed); each tag appears on its own row
params.metric: question_id = posts_questions.id | tag = TRIM(tag_extracted) where tag_extracted is each element produced by UNNEST(REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(COALESCE(posts_questions.tags, ''), r'<([^>]+)>'))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base (NORM) on question_id = id — safe because this view is one row per question-tag and questions_base is one row per question; joining preserves one-to-many semantics (question -> multiple tags) but does NOT duplicate question-level aggregates if questions_base contains only one row per question. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to question_answer_counts (AGG) or post_votes_agg (AGG) on question_id = question_id (or question_id = id as applicable) — safe when those aggregates are defined one-row-per-question because this view's rows expand tags but the aggregate measures are at question granularity; when computing tag-level aggregates, aggregate after the join to avoid double-counting. | do NOT blindly join to answers_base (NORM), comments_base (NORM), or any other one-to-many child (e.g., answers, comments) without re-aggregation, because those joins create a multi-way one-to-many expansion (question -> tags and question -> answers) that will multiply rows and thereby duplicate question-level measures. If you need combined info (e.g., questions x answers x tags), either: | - aggregate answers/comments to one row per question first (e.g., use answers_ranked_by_score_per_question or question_answer_counts) and then join to this tag view, or | - join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY tag and compute COUNT(DISTINCT question_id) or SUM of question-level measures with appropriate DISTINCT handling). | When composing into tag-level metrics (e.g., questions_per_tag, avg_answers_per_tag): join this view to question-level aggregates and then GROUP BY tag to compute sums/averages. Avoid computing question-level aggregates after joining to answers/comments without using DISTINCT or re-aggregation, as that will over-count.

question_tag_exploded.description: Explodes the tags string on questions into one row per (question_id, tag). Useful for per-tag aggregations or tag-level trend analysis. Assumes tags are whitespace/delimited with angle brackets as in typical StackOverflow exports (e.g. '<sql><bigquery>'). | Use for: tag popularity over time; top tags by question count or aggregate score; join tag-level metrics back to questions or answers

answers_ranked_by_score_per_question.name: answers_ranked_by_score_per_question
answers_ranked_by_score_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.parent_id AS question_id,
  a.score AS answer_score,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_date,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.parent_id ORDER BY a.score DESC, a.creation_date ASC, a.id ASC) AS answer_rank,
  CASE WHEN ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.parent_id ORDER BY a.score DESC, a.creation_date ASC, a.id ASC) = 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_top_answer
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per answer_id with rank within question_id

params.description: Provides one row per answer with its rank (within its question) by score, plus whether it is the top answer for that question.
params.when_to_use: Find the top (highest-scored) answer for each question | Retrieve answers ordered or filtered by their rank within the question (e.g., top 3 answers per question) | Join answer-level metadata with rank information for downstream aggregation (e.g., count of top answers by user) | Compose queries that need a stable deterministic ordering of answers within each question (score desc, creation_date asc, id asc)
params.output_schema: answer_id: the primary id of the answer (derived from posts_answers.id) | question_id: the parent question id this answer belongs to (derived from posts_answers.parent_id) | answer_score: the score/votes of the answer (derived from posts_answers.score) | answer_creation_date: timestamp when the answer was created (derived from posts_answers.creation_date) | answer_rank: integer position of this answer within its question partition, computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_id ORDER BY score DESC, creation_date ASC, id ASC) | is_top_answer: boolean true when answer_rank = 1 for that question (derived from the same ROW_NUMBER() expression)
params.metric: answer_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_id ORDER BY score DESC, creation_date ASC, id ASC) | is_top_answer = CASE WHEN answer_rank = 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to questions_base (or questions_with_user) on question_id = questions_base.id — safe because this view has one row per answer (answer_id) and joining to the question (one row per question) will not duplicate answer-level rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on posts_answers.owner_user_id = users_base.id (note: owner_user_id is not a column in this view; to use it you must join the answers_base/answers_source that includes owner_user_id, or join this view to answers_base first on answer_id) — joining this view to a users dimension (one row per user) is safe and will not duplicate answer rows. | do NOT directly join to any one-to-many tables without re-aggregation: for example, do NOT join this view to comments_base (which contains multiple comment rows per answer_id) or to post_votes_agg if it is not pre-aggregated by answer_id, because those joins would multiply answer rows and thus duplicate measures derived at the answer grain. If you need combined metrics (e.g., comment_count per answer), pre-aggregate the many-side by answer_id (e.g., SELECT answer_id, COUNT(*) AS comment_count FROM comments_base GROUP BY answer_id) and then join the aggregated result to this view on answer_id. | When joining to sibling aggregated views (post_votes_agg, question_answer_counts): ensure the aggregate view is keyed at a compatible grain. For example, joining answers_ranked_by_score_per_question to post_votes_agg is safe only if post_votes_agg has one row per answer_id; joining to question_answer_counts (one row per question) is safe when joined on question_id because question_answer_counts is one-row-per-question and will not duplicate answer rows. | If you need to produce metrics aggregated by question (for example, count of top answers by tag), re-aggregate at the question-level after joining: e.g., SELECT question_id, SUM(CASE WHEN is_top_answer THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS top_answer_count FROM answers_ranked_by_score_per_question GROUP BY question_id. Avoid joining this view to a many-side and then aggregating without proper GROUP BY to preserve correct counts. | Note on determinism: answer_rank uses ORDER BY score DESC, creation_date ASC, id ASC to ensure deterministic tie-breaking. Any composition that re-orders or re-partitions should preserve these columns if consistent ranking is required.

answers_ranked_by_score_per_question.description: Ranks answers within each parent question by score descending and provides rank and is_top_answer flag. Useful to select top-N answers per question deterministically downstream by filtering on answer_rank. | Use for: select top-N answers per question; compare top answer characteristics to others; compute metrics for accepted vs top-scoring answers

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS src
CROSS JOIN UNNEST(
  -- split the tags string like "<tag1><tag2>" into individual tags
  REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(COALESCE(src.tags, ''), r'<([^>]+)>')
) AS tag
-- carry canonical question id into output
JOIN (
  -- project the question_id from available questions_base-like fields
  SELECT id AS question_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
) AS q
ON q.question_id = src.id
WHERE COALESCE(src.post_type_id, 1) = 1
  AND tag IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(tag) <> ''
tags_extracted_from_posts.description: Exploded view mapping each question post to its individual tags (one row per post_id + tag). Parses the Stack Overflow angle-bracket tag format into separate canonical tag names (lowercased), enabling accurate whole-tag matching and tag-level aggregations.

posts_text_normalized.name: posts_text_normalized

answers_canonical.name: answers_canonical

SELECT
  -- primary key of the answer post
  a.id AS answer_id,
  -- parent question id (ensure numeric)
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_question_id,
  -- author user id (may be NULL)
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  -- numeric score (ensure INT64)
  CAST(a.score AS INT64) AS score,
  -- creation timestamp of the answer
  a.creation_date AS creation_date,
  -- whether this answer is the accepted answer for its parent question
  CASE
    WHEN a.id IS NOT NULL
     AND q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL
     AND CAST(q.accepted_answer_id AS INT64) = a.id THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS is_accepted_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
ON CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) = q.id
WHERE
  -- keep only answer posts (post_type_id for answers is typically 2 in StackOverflow schema;
  -- lift literal if you want to change filtering outside the view)
  a.post_type_id = 2
  -- optionally exclude anonymous/unknown owners by uncommenting the next line in consuming SQL:
  -- AND a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL

  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  q.tags AS tags,

  -- typed / normalized numeric fields (some source columns are STRING in DDL)
  SAFE_CAST(q.answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  SAFE_CAST(q.view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  SAFE_CAST(q.score AS INT64) AS score,

  -- computed
  -- body_length: number of characters in body (NULL preserved if body is NULL)
  IFNULL(CHAR_LENGTH(q.body), 0) AS body_length

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q

users_with_badge_and_netvotes.name: users_with_badge_and_netvotes
users_with_badge_and_netvotes.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  u.up_votes AS up_votes,
  u.down_votes AS down_votes,
  (COALESCE(u.up_votes, 0) - COALESCE(u.down_votes, 0)) AS net_votes,
  COALESCE(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(1) AS badge_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.badges`
  GROUP BY
    user_id
) AS b
ON u.id = b.user_id
